questions.question: What are Voyager's three core components?
options: Memory, Planning, Execution
Automatic curriculum, Skill library, Iterative prompting mechanism
Proposer, Critic, Refiner
Planner, Worker, Solver
questions.explanation: Voyager (Wang et al., TMLR 2024) has three components: an Automatic curriculum (curiosity-driven task proposer), a Skill library (executable code stored and retrieved by similarity), and an Iterative prompting mechanism (refine skills using environment feedback).

questions.question: Why does Voyager use code as its action space instead of primitive commands?
options: Code is faster to execute than primitive commands
Code enables temporally extended, composable, reusable behavior that can be stored as named skills and retrieved later
Code requires fewer tokens than listing primitive commands
Primitive commands are not supported in Minecraft
questions.explanation: Making the action space code (JavaScript functions) enables temporally extended actions, composition from sub-skills, and storage as retrievable named programs. This is the foundation for the 2026 Claude Agent SDK skills pattern.

questions.question: What three feedback signals does Voyager's iterative prompting mechanism use?
options: Reward, Penalty, Neutral
Success, Error (with stack trace), Self-verification failure
Pass, Fail, Retry
High, Medium, Low confidence
questions.explanation: Voyager's feedback loop uses three signals: success (skill works as intended), error with stack trace (execution failed), and self-verification failure (skill ran but did not achieve the goal). All three feed back into skill refinement.

questions.question: What Minecraft performance improvements does Voyager report vs baselines?
options: 2x more unique items, 3x faster stone tools
3.3x more unique items, 8.5x faster stone tools, 6.4x faster iron tools, 2.3x longer map traversal
5x faster task completion, 10x better success rate
Same performance, but with far fewer tokens
questions.explanation: Voyager achieves 3.3x more unique items, 8.5x faster stone tools, 6.4x faster iron tools, and 2.3x longer map traversal versus baselines in Minecraft (Wang et al., 2024).

questions.question: What is 'skill library rot' and how is it mitigated?
options: Skills becoming outdated as the environment changes; mitigate by re-running all skills periodically
The same skill being added multiple times with slightly different descriptions; mitigate by deduplication on write
Skills taking too long to execute; mitigate by adding timeouts
Skills conflicting with each other; mitigate by version pinning
questions.explanation: Skill library rot means the same skill gets added 10+ times with slightly different descriptions, bloating the library and degrading retrieval. Deduplication on write — collapsing near-duplicate descriptions to one canonical skill — prevents this.

questions.question: How does the Voyager skill retrieval process work for a new task?
options: The agent reads all skills and picks the most recently added one
The task description is embedded, top-k similar skills are retrieved, and the new skill is composed from retrieved primitives plus new logic
The agent asks the user which skill to use
Skills are retrieved alphabetically until one works
questions.explanation: For a new task: (1) embed the task description, (2) query the skill library for top-k similar skills, (3) retrieve relevant primitives, (4) compose a new skill from those primitives plus any new logic needed.
